requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. above need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions.
ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.
ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the limits shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit remains constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit remains constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m shall be below the type approval limits.
The emission of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The maximum allowed pulse amplitude of positive polarity for vehicles with 12 V systems shall be +75 V.
The maximum allowed pulse amplitude of negative polarity for vehicles with 12 V systems shall be -100 V.
The maximum allowed pulse amplitude of positive polarity for vehicles with 24 V systems shall be +150 V.
The maximum allowed pulse amplitude of negative polarity for vehicles with 24 V systems shall be -450 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9: Test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a; test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): Stripline, 20 to 400 MHz, 60 V/m.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz, 75 V/m.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): BCI, 20 to 400 MHz, 60 mA.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz, 30 V/m.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): ALSE, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, 10 V/m.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): Reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz, 21 V/m.
Test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2a): Reverberation chamber, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, 7 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): Stripline, 20 to 400 MHz, 50 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): TEM cell, 20 to 200 MHz, 62,5 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): BCI, 20 to 400 MHz, 50 mA.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): ALSE, 80 to 2,000 MHz, 25 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): ALSE, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, 8 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): Reverberation chamber, LUF to 2,000 MHz, 18 V/m.
Minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band (Table 2b): Reverberation chamber, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, 6 V/m.

The ESA representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
Starting profile shall be tested according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

Starting profile: immunity test level II for 12 V system and II for 24 V system, 10 pulses; functional status B for immunity related functions (for ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases), C for immunity related functions (for other ESA), and D for functions not related to immunity related functions. Starting profile is only applicable to ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

Test pulse 1: immunity test level -75 V for 12 V system and -450 V for 24 V system, 500 pulses; FPSC III for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
Test pulse 2a: immunity test level +37 V for 12 V system and +37 V for 24 V system, 500 pulses; FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
Test pulse 2b: immunity test level +10 V for 12 V system and +20 V for 24 V system, 10 pulses; FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Test pulse 3a: immunity test level -112 V for 12 V system and -150 V for 24 V system, test duration 1 h; FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

Test pulse 3b: immunity test level +75 V for 12 V system and +150 V for 24 V system, test duration 1 h; FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
Where an ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.
ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).

Vehicles or components or ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7. above.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to broadband electromagnetic disturbances if the levels measured do not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1. above for ESAs.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to narrowband electromagnetic disturbances if the levels measured do not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1. above for ESAs.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to immunity to electromagnetic radiation if the ESA does not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1. for ESAs above.

If the conformity of a component, or Separate Technical Unit (STU) taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to immunity to conducted disturbances if the component or STU shows no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1. above.

If the conformity of a component, or Separate Technical Unit (STU) taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to emission if the component or STU does not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1. above.
ESA broadband reference limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 30-75 MHz band: E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
ESA broadband reference limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 75-400 MHz band: E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
ESA broadband reference limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 400-1,000 MHz band: E = 63 (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).
The limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 30-75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) (See paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation).
The limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 75-400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) (See paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation).
The limit E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth in the 400-1,000 MHz frequency band shall be E = 53 (See paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation).
For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN as defined in Figure 1 shall be used.
The AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the AN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
Measurement ports of AN(s) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
The AN impedance ZPB (tolerance ± 20 %) in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz is shown in Figure 2.
If not otherwise stated in this Annex the test shall be performed according CISPR 25.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" the test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) an open area test site (OATS), which complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
To ensure that there is no extraneous noise or signal of a magnitude sufficient to affect materially the measurement, measurements shall be taken before or after the main test.

In this measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
If peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
Unless otherwise specified the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
If not otherwise stated in this Annex the test shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The test shall be performed according to ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) an open area test site (OATS) which complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 may be used.
To ensure that there is no extraneous noise or signal of a magnitude sufficient to affect materially the measurement, measurements shall be taken before or after the main test.

In this measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
Measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video band width shall be at least three times the resolution band width (RBW).
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

ESAs may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
Frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on.
The ESA under test shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase.
No extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.

To ensure reproducible measurement results are obtained when tests and measurements are repeated, the test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit and the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
Measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
Frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
If an ESA fails the tests defined in this Annex, the ESA shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
The "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
The test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
The test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.

The test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench with the following characteristics: BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA; or BCI test method with closed loop method and injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.

As an alternative the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the following characteristics: BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
The test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
The test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing method shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
This test method shall ensure the immunity of ESAs to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
This test method shall limit conducted transients from ESAs to the vehicle power supply.
Apply the test pulse 1 according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Apply the test pulse 2a according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Apply the test pulse 2b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Apply the test pulse 3a according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Apply the test pulse 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Apply the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 to the supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines: measurement according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
This sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall consist of a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "D" shall be placed on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
If applicable, to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4., the additional letter "Y" shall be placed on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
On lamps with reduced light distribution, see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, the approval marking shall consist of a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources.
Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with an electronic light source control gear.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
In any case the approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both, the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.2. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.4. shall be affixed on the lamp.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
The conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval shall apply to this Regulation.

The requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps must be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to rear position lamps.
An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to stop lamps.
An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to rear position lamps.
An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to stop lamps.

Position lamps which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, are permitted.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

The internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo build by transparent or non-transparent components provided that all requirements for the specific function of this Regulation are fulfilled.
Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed.
The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) of such a lamp in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following provisions shall apply: (a) The light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) A signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.

The lamp shall only be equipped with: replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061.
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that the light source module is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of device shall be met.
All measurements, photometric and colorimetric, shall be made with respect to the conditions of paragraph 4.8.1. (Particulars of the methods of measurement to be used are given in Annex 3).
In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.
If not otherwise specified, the intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.

In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver viewed from the reference centre of the light is comprised between 10' and 1 degree.

In case the results of measurements should be challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed to be satisfied if that requirement is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.
The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, in the case of light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) the lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed.

The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

Retro-reflective devices must be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.
The resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not more than the value in Table 10.
Before measuring, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
The reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After having brushed in the case of moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA the rear face of the retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture, defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
The RI shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
The apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The apparatus shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity.
The apparatus shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1, in case of retro-reflective devices for a period of 500 hours.
Preparation of test specimens shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied for a retro-reflective device.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
After about five minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually.
The surface of the retro-reflective device must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.
After about 5 minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
The RI shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The approval number must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number must face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class must be diametrically opposite the approval number.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
For all light-signalling devices, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road.
The reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle in the case of all other signalling devices.
In each direction a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the rear of the vehicle.
All logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical the above requirements shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Lamps may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, shall be installed in such a way that: (a) Either the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; or (b) The minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
The maximum height above the ground shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
The minimum height above the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground, shall be measured from the H plane.

The position, as regards width, will be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width.
The position, as regards width, will be determined from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary in relation to the ambient light, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement above shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp is the following: White.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp is the following: Red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp is the following: Red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, is the following: Red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Any lamp may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

Rear position lamps may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position requirements for those lamps.

Rear position lamps may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the geometric visibility requirements for those lamps.

Rear position lamps may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the colorimetric requirements for those lamps.

Rear position lamps may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the photometric requirements for those lamps.

Rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the retro-reflectors on the movable components meet all the position requirements for those lamps.

Rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the retro-reflectors on the movable components meet all the geometric visibility requirements for those lamps.

Rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the retro-reflectors on the movable components meet all the colorimetric requirements for those lamps.

Rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the retro-reflectors on the movable components meet all the photometric requirements for those lamps.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of rear position lamps shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for retro-reflectors shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement of paragraph 5.21 is not practicable, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp even bearing an approval mark is deemed not to be present when the lamp cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.
During replacement, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, which respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed, provided that the intensity of all the lamps mentioned above, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control are allowed, provided that in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to the following conditions: ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds, contamination of the light emitting surface.

Independent from environmental conditions mentioned under 5.26.1. a decrease of the luminous intensity, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m.
As long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h the intensity decrease already activated may remain active.
No sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.
It may be possible for the driver to set the functions above to static luminous intensities.

The voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the device may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity.
If measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.
A LED module does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle.
Presence of the reversing lamp: Mandatory on motor vehicles.
Number: One device mandatory and a second device optional on motor vehicles of category M1.
These devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
In height: not less than 250 mm above the ground.
In height: not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
In length: at the rear of the vehicle.
Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle: Geometric visibility defined by angles α and β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.: α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle: Geometric visibility defined by angles α and β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.: β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device.
Devices installed at the rear of the vehicle: Geometric visibility defined by angles α and β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.: β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two.
Orientation: Rearwards.

The electrical connections shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either of the above conditions is not satisfied.
Tell-tale optional, however a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Devices of S1 or S2 categories: mandatory on all categories of vehicles.
Two S1 or S2 category devices on all categories of vehicles.
The devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles: For S1 or S2 categories devices that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
For S1 or S2 categories devices: Above the ground, not less than 350 mm.

For S1 or S2 categories devices: Above the ground, not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
For S1 or S2 categories devices: at the rear of the vehicle.
Geometric visibility Horizontal angle: For S1 or S2 categories devices: 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

However, for the stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Vertical angle: For S1 or S2 categories devices: 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
Orientation Towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device, which starts and/or stops the propulsion system, is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
Tell-tale optional, however a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamp devices of R or R1 or R2 categories: Mandatory.

Number of rear position lamps: Two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

In width: that point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
In height: the rear position lamp shall be above the ground not less than 350 mm.

In height: the rear position lamp shall be above the ground not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
In length: the rear position lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
Geometric visibility of the rear position lamp: Horizontal angle: 45° inwards.
Geometric visibility of the rear position lamp: Horizontal angle: 80° outwards.
Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Geometric visibility of the rear position lamp: Vertical angle: 15° above the horizontal.
Geometric visibility of the rear position lamp: Vertical angle: 15° below the horizontal.
Where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, Horizontal angle: 45° outwards to 45° inwards.

Under the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2., where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
Under the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2., Vertical angle: 15° above and below the horizontal.

Under the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2., where a rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
To be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres.
The illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
Orientation of the rear position lamp: Rearwards.
Electrical connections of the rear position lamp: In accordance with paragraph 5.11.
Tell-tale for the rear position lamp: Closed-circuit tell-tale mandatory.
The closed-circuit tell-tale shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
Presence of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular: Mandatory on motor vehicles.
Number of rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular: Two.

The two rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4. below), are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
In width: that point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
In height: Above the ground, not less than 250 mm.

In height: Above the ground, not more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively).
In length: at the rear of the vehicle.
Geometric visibility: Horizontal angle: 30° inwards.
Geometric visibility: Horizontal angle: 30° outwards.
Geometric visibility: Vertical angle: 10° above horizontal.

Geometric visibility: Vertical angle: 10° below horizontal. However, where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Orientation: Rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. above.
In their respective planes, the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer are bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

In their respective planes, the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer are bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width.
If there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. of this Regulation, in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation.
The values measured for the distances shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
The angles of geometric visibility shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation.

The values measured for the angles shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.
The lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
